text:
Mika Patel: Heads up — BrightPay dedicated pool in eu-west-1 is doing a ping-pong scale pattern, customers report intermittent 429s and p95 jumps to ~2.5s. Attaching quick notes and repro.

Sean O'Connor: Saw this pop up on the dashboard, thanks. Any correlation with scheduled batch windows or nightly jobs?

Mika Patel: nope, traffic from the tenant is steady during the window. Autoscaler logs show scale-up then immediate scale-down within ~90s repeatedly.

Priya Nair: That sounds like cooldown / windowing is too tight. What's the existing cooldown config?

Evan Zhou: Current autoscaler snippet we use for that pool: 
```
autoscaler:
  target_cpu: 0.7
  scale_up_window: 30
  scale_down_window: 45
  cooldown: 60
```

Mika Patel: infra-bot posted telemetry: CPU spikes to ~85% at the start of a burst, then drops to ~20% after a new node joins. GPU memory and NVLink look fine. Request pattern is short bursts (10s) every minute.

Sean O'Connor: Could be a noisy neighbor doing a background job that coincides with the bursts? Any tenant-level CPU breakdown?

Mika Patel: We checked top processes — one tenant has periodic background workers at those times. But even after isolating their traffic into a separate pool, the autoscaler still oscillates (so not purely noisy neighbor).

Priya Nair: Two things to try: (1) increase cooldown (2) require consecutive windows before scaling up (hysteresis). Also consider a small overprovision of 1 node so short bursts don't trigger scaling.

Evan Zhou: I'll spin a staging patch with these changes. Proposed config: 
```
scale:
  cooldown: 300        # 5m
  scale_up_consecutive_windows: 2
  min_overprovision: 1
  utilization_aggregation_seconds: 120  # average over 2m
```

oncall-sre: Can we get a quick runbook entry? If this fixes it we'll push to prod off-hours.

Mika Patel: Also noticed the 429s are sometimes coming from per-tenant qps throttles firing when nodes briefly leave. That cascades into client retries / bursty behavior. @billing-bot confirmed no recent quota changes.

Sean O'Connor: Repro steps for SRE to validate: 1) replay the captured trace with loadgen (burst pattern), 2) tail `autoscaler:event` logs, 3) collect `/metrics` and `node_exporter` for 3-5 minutes, 4) check per-tenant throttle counters. I can handle the loadgen run.

Evan Zhou: Running the staging run now in eu-west-1 with the patched config, will post results in ~10m :eyes:

infra-bot: deploy started: config-patch/deploy-1868454 -> eu-west-1 (rolling) — logs: https://ci.internal/reports/deploy-1868454

Mika Patel: If the staging run stabilizes scale (no rapid downscales within 3m of scale-up) we should proceed to a gradual rollout.

Priya Nair: Follow-up note: long-term we should move to a smoothed utilization metric (exponential decay or sliding window) rather than instantaneous percent to avoid reacting to short-lived spikes. Adding to infra backlog.

Evan Zhou: Staging run complete: with cooldown=300 + consecutive windows, no scale ping-pong seen in the 20m test, p95 stayed under 800ms, no tenant qps throttle. Will prepare PR for prod change and runbook update.

oncall-sre: Thanks — I'll coordinate a midnight rollout and page CS if anything odd.

Mika Patel: Great work. After prod patch, let's keep 24h of elevated telemetry retention for that pool to ensure no regressions.

billing-bot: Note: no quota or billing events detected for tenant during timeframe.
